inline_comments.comment:
The second assertion in the 'should rank affected above modified and below warning' test uses `'status-value:modified'` instead of `'status-value:affected'`:
```ts
expect(getMostCriticalStatusValue(['status-value:modified', 'status-value:warning'])).toBe('status-value:warning');
```
This tests that `warning > modified`, which is already proved by the pre-existing 'should return the highest status' test. The test name promises that `affected < warning`, but this assertion never verifies that. Change the array to `['status-value:affected', 'status-value:warning']` to actually exercise the claimed behavior.

`@default true` is incorrect. The actual default is `false`, set in `common-preset.ts` (`changeDetection: false`). The dev server reads this flag as `features?.changeDetection !== false` to enable full change detection, meaning an absent/`undefined` value also enables it—but the explicit preset default overrides that to `false`. The JSDoc annotation should read `@default false` to accurately document the out-of-the-box behavior.

`affected` is given `theme.color.warning` as its icon color, which is identical to the color used for `status-value:warning`. Despite having a lower priority in `statusPriority`, the two statuses will be visually indistinguishable in the sidebar. Users will not be able to tell at a glance whether an item is 'affected by a change' or 'has a test warning'. Consider a distinct color (e.g., `theme.color.secondary` or an orange shade distinct from warning's yellow) so both icons communicate different urgency levels.

All three new status values are given `theme.fgColor.accent` here, but `status.tsx`'s `getStatus` assigns them distinct colors (`theme.color.positive` for `new`, `theme.color.secondary` for `modified`, `theme.color.warning` for `affected`). These two code paths are used in different rendering contexts within the same sidebar, so the same status can appear in different colors depending on which component renders it. Consolidate by driving both from `getStatus`—similar to how `StatusButton` in the current codebase already calls `getStatus(theme, status).iconColor`—rather than maintaining a parallel color map.

The priority ordering places `modified` (direct code edit) *below* `affected` (indirect dependency change): `unknown < pending < success < modified < affected < new`. Semantically this is questionable—a directly modified story file arguably warrants more attention than one that is only transitively affected. Consider reversing the order to `affected < modified < new` so that more directly changed stories surface higher in aggregated group status.

The `NEW_ID` and `MODIFIED_ID` symbols include comments linking to their source in the `storybookjs/icons` repository (e.g., `// https://github.com/storybookjs/icons/blob/main/src/icons/AddIcon.tsx`). The `AFFECTED_ID` symbol only has a description comment (`// Ripple/wave icon for affected stories`) with no link or attribution. Either source the icon from the icons library and add the link, or add a comment noting it is a custom illustration, so future maintainers know where to update it if the design changes.

general_comments.comment: No stories are added for the three new `StatusValue` variants. Per project rules, interactive sidebar components with new states should have story `play` functions that exercise the open/expanded state so it is captured in visual regression tests. At minimum, add story variants (or update existing `StatusButton` / `IconSymbols` stories) that show each of `new`, `modified`, and `affected` states—including their icon and color—and include `play` functions that validate the rendered output. Without stories it is impossible to visually review or regression-test the new icons and colors.

The test suite adds coverage for `new` and `affected` propagating through group aggregation, but there is no equivalent test for `status-value:modified`. Since `modified` sits between `affected` and `new` in the priority chain, a story covering it follows the same pattern and the omission is likely an oversight rather than a deliberate choice.

The PR description states 'Updated the vitest addon's `statusValueToStoryIds` map to include the new values,' but the actual change does the opposite: it explicitly excludes the new values by introducing the `TestStatusValue` Extract type that omits `new`, `modified`, and `affected`. The description should be corrected to avoid confusion for reviewers and future git-blame readers.
